summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped), so there are no Studio outputs, no transient trace and no numerical comparison. The selected scenario is Figure 9 of W3086153377, a thermal-aware redundant-TSV insertion study for a 4x4x4 (64-core) 3D-NoC. Per-router HotSpot 6.0 temperatures feed a Black's-model normalized fault rate relative to the coolest area, and results are given as redundancy counts and MTTF relative to targets of 1.5x, 2x and 2.5x MTTF at Tref. The extraction proposed a custom_2d_steady experiment with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, which fails the input gate (needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). The paper has no bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers were used. No generated placement, input.flp or input.ptrace was produced, so there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The deterministic gate set simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false, so the final verdict is that this paper cannot be assessed with the 2D Studio. The paper reports no absolute temperature, so no paper value exists to compare against even in principle. Only qualitative reasoning is possible: hotter routers have a higher normalized fault rate and need more redundant TSVs. This is a 3D reliability study, not a 2D thermal experiment, and no exact replication is claimed.

The paper is a 3D-IC (4x4x4 TSV-based stack) TSV lifetime-reliability study, not a 2D chiplet or interposer thermal experiment. A 2D steady-state Studio model cannot represent the vertical layer coupling, inter-layer temperature differences or TSV thermal paths.

The paper publishes no floorplan: no block coordinates, dimensions or per-block or per-router watts. The power map and floorplan used for HotSpot are not given in the text (Step 2 on PDF page 12 only mentions them), so no same-scenario geometry and power rows can be built.

The workload is derived from PARSEC switching activity from gem5 and varies over time and by benchmark, while the thermal result is only a relative fault rate; no absolute temperature is published to compare against.

The principal contributions are the IaSiG hardware fault-detection method (parity check, isolation and shift) and the grid-search redundancy insertion. These are digital reliability mechanisms with WCET in cycles, not thermal management controllers or optimizers, and do not map to a Studio thermal controller or placement optimizer.

The cooling configuration, package and HotSpot 6.0 parameters (layer stack, TSV thermal modelling, heat sink, ambient) are not published in the paper. The paper notes TSV insertion slightly changes temperature but ignores it.

The reliability metric (Black's-model normalized fault rate and MTTF, Eq. 17-18) and its parameters (Ea, current density exponent) are outside a thermal solver and are not reproduced by a steady-state temperature calculation.
